newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia street children get $7.05 million from EU.
newsitem.headline: Colombia street children get $7.05 million from EU.

text.p: The European Union will donate $7.05 million to help Colombia's growing population of street children, officials said on Wednesday.

The money will be combined with $1.4 million donated by the Colombian government and independent aid organizations to set up projects to combat homelessness, drug addiction and sexual abuse affecting street children in the country's major cities, an EU statement said.
The EU's delegation in Colombia estimates that more than two-thirds of Colombians under the age of 18 are living in poverty and believes 15,000 children are living on the streets.
"Behind these numbers are countless stories of misery, delinquency, prostitution, sexual abuse, malnutrition and sickness," EU representative in Colombia Jaime Cavanillas said in the statement.
The EU has granted more than $13.9 million to Colombia so far this year, including $5 million to aid the thousands of Colombians displaced by the country's protracted guerrilla war, the EU said.
